Brand & content

Explore related services↗
#

Art direction

The creative decisions that give a shoot or campaign a consistent visual style, including composition, lighting, colours and props.

#

Brand communication

The messages a business shares with its audience. Clear communication connects what the business offers with what its customers need.

#

Brand guidelines

A practical set of rules for using a brand consistently across websites, packaging, social posts and other communication.

#

Brand identity

The visual and verbal elements that help people recognise a business: its logo, colours, typography, imagery and tone of voice.

#

Brand positioning

The place a business aims to occupy in its audience’s mind. It explains who the offer is for, what problem it solves and why someone should choose it.

#

Call to action (CTA)

A prompt that tells a visitor what to do next, such as book a call, request a quote or explore a service.

#

Content calendar

A schedule of planned posts and campaigns. It helps a team coordinate topics, formats, approvals and publishing dates.

#

Content marketing

Creating and sharing useful information that helps an audience understand a topic or make a decision. Articles, videos and guides are common formats.

#

Copywriting

Writing words for a specific communication goal, such as explaining a product, encouraging an enquiry or introducing a brand.

#

Motion graphics

Graphic elements brought to life through animation. They can explain an idea, introduce a brand or make a message easier to follow.

SEO & AI search

Explore related services↗
#

Answer engine optimization (AEO)

Structuring clear answers to user questions so search and answer systems can understand the information. Inclusion in an answer is not guaranteed.

#

Backlink

A link from another website to yours. Relevant links can help people discover your content; the quality and context of the linking page matter.

#

Canonical URL

The preferred address for a page when similar content is available at more than one URL. A canonical tag is a signal to search engines about which version to use.

#

Crawling & indexing

Crawling is a search engine discovering and reading a page. Indexing is its decision to store that page for possible inclusion in search results.

#

Generative engine optimization (GEO)

Improving the clarity, credibility and accessibility of information for AI-assisted discovery. No provider can guarantee that an AI system will cite a particular business.

#

Internal link

A link connecting pages or sections within the same website. It helps visitors explore related information and search engines discover content.

#

Keyword research

Finding the words and questions an audience uses when searching. This helps shape useful page topics and content that answers real needs.

#

Local SEO

Improving visibility for location-based searches. Accurate business details, a suitable business profile and useful local information are part of the work.

#

Meta description

A short description in a page’s HTML that search engines may use in results. It should clearly explain what a visitor can expect to find.

#

On-page SEO

Improving the content and elements of a page, including its title, headings, descriptions, images and internal links.

#

Organic traffic

Visits from unpaid search results. Organic visibility depends on relevance, website quality, competition and other search signals.

#

Search engine optimization (SEO)

Improving a website’s content, structure and technical quality so search engines can understand it and people can find relevant pages in unpaid search results.

#

Search intent

The purpose behind a search: learning, comparing options, finding a particular website or taking an action. A useful page should match that purpose.

#

Structured data

Machine-readable information describing a page’s content. It helps search engines understand entities such as an organisation, a term or a question.

#

Technical SEO

Work that helps search engines access and understand a website. Examples include checking crawlability, page speed, canonical URLs and structured data.

#

XML sitemap

A structured file listing the preferred URLs on a website. It helps search engines discover pages, but does not guarantee indexing or rankings.

Paid media & campaigns

Explore related services↗
#

Click-through rate (CTR)

The percentage of impressions that result in a click. Calculate it as clicks divided by impressions, multiplied by 100.

#

Cost per click (CPC)

The average advertising cost for each click. Calculate it as ad spend divided by the number of clicks.

#

Cost per lead (CPL)

The average campaign cost for each recorded lead. Lead quality and the definition of a lead should be reviewed alongside this number.

#

Impressions

The number of times content or an ad is displayed. The same person may create multiple impressions.

#

Media buying

Planning and purchasing advertising placements to reach an audience, including decisions about channels, formats, timing and budgets.

#

Pay-per-click (PPC)

An advertising model in which the advertiser pays when someone clicks an ad. Costs and results depend on the platform, audience and campaign setup.

#

Performance marketing

Marketing planned around measurable actions, such as enquiries or purchases. Campaigns are reviewed using agreed goals, budgets and reporting.

#

Reach

The number of distinct people or accounts estimated to have seen content during a period. It differs from impressions, which count repeated views.

#

Retargeting

Advertising to people who have already interacted with a business. It requires suitable platform setup, audience permissions and privacy controls.

#

Return on ad spend (ROAS)

Revenue attributed to ads divided by advertising spend. A 4× ROAS means four units of attributed revenue per unit spent; it is not the same as profit.

Social & creators

Explore related services↗
#

Community management

Responding to and moderating audience conversations on a brand’s channels within an agreed response and escalation process.

#

Creator brief

A document explaining a campaign’s goal, audience, key message, content requirements, deadlines and approval process.

#

Engagement rate

A measure of interactions such as comments, saves or likes relative to an audience or reach figure. Different platforms use different calculation methods.

#

Influencer marketing

Working with creators to communicate a brand message to a relevant audience. A campaign should agree deliverables, disclosures, timings and usage rights.

#

Online reputation management

Monitoring and responding to public feedback about a business. It focuses on clear communication and issue handling rather than inventing positive reviews.

#

Social media handling

The ongoing planning, creation, publishing and management of a business’s social profiles. The agreed scope can also include replies and performance reports.

#

Usage rights

Permission to use creative work in specific ways, channels, markets and periods. Posting content does not automatically grant unlimited rights.

#

User-generated content (UGC)

Content created by users or creators rather than the brand’s own team. Commissioned creator content can be used by a brand when the required rights are agreed.

Websites & e-commerce

Explore related services↗
#

Accessibility

Designing content and interactions so people with different abilities can use them. Examples include readable contrast, keyboard access and meaningful image descriptions.

#

Content management system (CMS)

Software that lets authorised people manage website content without editing every page directly in code.

#

Conversion rate optimization (CRO)

Improving a website or journey to help more suitable visitors complete a desired action. Changes should be based on research and measured where possible.

#

E-commerce website

A website that supports online product browsing and purchasing. Common features include product pages, a cart, payment integration and order management.

#

Landing page

A page focused on a particular campaign or audience need. Its content and call to action should support one clear next step.

#

Responsive design

A design approach that adapts a website to different screen sizes so its content and controls remain usable.

#

User experience (UX)

How a person experiences a website or product while completing a task. Clear navigation, useful information and accessible forms contribute to good UX.

#

User interface (UI)

The visible controls and layout people interact with, including buttons, menus, forms and page components.

Measurement & growth

Explore related services↗
#

A/B testing

Comparing two versions of an element or experience to learn which performs better against an agreed metric. Useful results need enough suitable data.

#

Attribution

The method used to assign credit for a conversion to marketing interactions. Different models may report different results for the same journey.

#

Conversion

An action a business chooses to measure, such as a form submission, a purchase or a booking. The definition should be agreed before reporting begins.

#

Conversion rate

The percentage of measured visits or interactions that lead to a conversion. The denominator and reporting period should be stated.

#

Key performance indicator (KPI)

A metric selected to track progress toward a business goal. An enquiry campaign and a brand-awareness campaign usually need different KPIs.

#

Lead generation

Attracting and collecting enquiries from potential customers. A good lead process considers suitability, consent and follow-up as well as volume.

#

Marketing automation

Using defined rules to trigger marketing or follow-up tasks, such as sending an approved message after an enquiry.

#

UTM parameters

Labels added to campaign URLs to identify a source, medium or campaign in reporting. They help distinguish traffic from different marketing activities.
